correctness.rationale: The rank-two T_a formulas exactly detect capped colour counts within E1; the rank-four U_b formulas exactly detect capped counts of E1 classes within E2. A two-pebble guarded partial-isomorphism family on singleton and E2-related pairs has explicit forth/back extensions sharing zero, one or two elements, so it preserves all GF sentences including on infinite domains. Conversely the rank-five Θ_S sentences distinguish each profile set. The minimal S-model contains one outer class of each b with exactly b_a inner classes of minimal size w(a); the sum gives μ(S), and taking all b gives the sharp universal bound. Independently executed finite greatest-fixed-point game checks 7335 comparisons and exact combinatorial arithmetic.

originality.rationale: Checked the precise profile-equivalence statement, its rank-five normal form, exact number of complete theories and sharp per-theory size against the recent nested-equivalence paper and closely related two-variable work. The 2026 paper treats general (also non-unary) signatures and complexity rather than an equality-allowed unary-only complete-theory classification; the 2025 FO2 theorem supplies a formula-length-dependent finite-model bound in a different, more expressive syntax, not the present formula-independent sharp GF bound. Published guarded-bisimulation machinery is acknowledged, not novel. Targeted published-finding corpus queries yielded no identical/superseding statement among returned closest hits. Priority is qualified rather than asserted exhaustive.

value.rationale: A complete and exact theory space for hierarchical equivalence data is mathematically natural in light of recent GF nested-equivalence work. The theorem gives all complete GF theories, exact minimum canonical size for each, a sharp formula-independent model bound, a rank-five collapse and size-spectrum generating polynomial; these jointly constitute structural information beyond generic decidability or the one-equivalence case. The object/invariant motivation is class hierarchy visibility under guarded quantifiers, and the numerical bounds are forced naturally by simultaneous realization of all logical types.
